questions.title: E-Commerce Order Total
questions.objective: Detect multiplication overflow with Math.multiplyExact() and handle the resulting ArithmeticException.
questions.problem_statement:
An online store calculates the total cost of a customer's order. The input provides a product price in paise, the quantity ordered, and the amount paid. The application must validate the order and calculate the change without overflowing a long.

Read three integers: price, quantity, and payment. Apply these checks in order:
1. If the price or quantity is not positive, or the payment is negative, print Invalid order.
2. If multiplying the price by the quantity would exceed Long.MAX_VALUE, print Order total overflow.
3. If the payment is less than the order total, print Insufficient payment.
Otherwise, print Order confirmed followed by the change due. Use Math.multiplyExact() to detect multiplication overflow and catch ArithmeticException. Do not print a confirmation for an invalid order.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, including custom exceptions, without the public keyword.

Explanation: The total is 2500 × 3 = 7500 paise. The customer pays 10000 paise, so the change due is 2500 paise.
questions.input_format: One line containing three space-separated integers: price in paise, quantity, and payment in paise.
questions.output_format:
On success, print two lines:
Order confirmed
Change due: <change>
On failure, print only the applicable error message.
questions.constraints:
Price and payment are valid Java long values.
1 ≤ quantity ≤ 1,000,000,000
hints: Read all three values as long.
Math.multiplyExact(price, quantity) throws ArithmeticException instead of silently wrapping around.
Put the multiplication in a try block and print Order total overflow in the catch block.

extra_fields.input_format: One line containing three space-separated integers: price in paise, quantity, and payment in paise.
extra_fields.output_format:
On success, print two lines:
Order confirmed
Change due: <change>
On failure, print only the applicable error message.

questions.title: Safely Parse a Customer Age
questions.objective: Catch NumberFormatException from Integer.parseInt() and then validate the parsed value.
questions.problem_statement:
A registration system receives a customer's age as text. Convert the entire input line to a Java int using Integer.parseInt().

The input must contain a valid decimal integer representation. An optional leading + or - sign is allowed, but at least one digit must follow the sign. Leading or trailing whitespace is invalid and must not be removed with trim(). Empty input, letters, decimal points, and values outside the Java int range must also be rejected.

If parsing succeeds, check the age. Print Invalid age if the age is below 0 or above 120. Otherwise, print Age accepted. If parsing fails, catch NumberFormatException and print Invalid integer.

If the environment provides no line at all, treat it as invalid input. Print exactly one result line.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, including custom exceptions, without the public keyword.

Explanation: Integer.parseInt("+25") returns 25. This value is within the permitted age range, so the registration system accepts it.
questions.input_format: One line containing the age as text. The line may be empty.
questions.output_format: Print Age accepted, Invalid age, or Invalid integer.
questions.constraints:
The input line contains at most 100 characters.
A successfully parsed integer must fit in the Java int range.
hints: Read the whole line with sc.nextLine(); check sc.hasNextLine() first in case there is no line.
Integer.parseInt() throws NumberFormatException for spaces, letters, an empty string, and out-of-range values.
Check the age range only after parsing succeeds, inside the try block.

extra_fields.input_format: One line containing the age as text. The line may be empty.
extra_fields.output_format: Print Age accepted, Invalid age, or Invalid integer.

questions.title: Retrieve a Warehouse Shelf Item
questions.objective: Access an array inside a try block and handle ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
questions.problem_statement:
A warehouse stores item quantities in an array. Each position represents a shelf number starting from zero. The program receives the number of shelves, the quantity stored on each shelf, and a requested shelf index.

Attempt to retrieve the quantity at the requested index. If the index is valid, print Quantity: followed by a space and the stored quantity. If the index is negative or greater than or equal to the array length, catch ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and print Invalid shelf index.

The array access must occur inside a try block, and the exception must be handled using catch. Do not replace the required exception-handling demonstration with only an if statement.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, including custom exceptions, without the public keyword.

Explanation: Shelf index 2 contains 20 items. Since index 2 is valid for an array of length 4, the program prints that quantity.
questions.input_format:
First line: integer N.
Second line: N space-separated quantities.
Third line: requested index K.
questions.output_format: Print Quantity: <value> or Invalid shelf index.
hints: Read the quantities into an int array of length N.
Put shelves[k] inside try; Java throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException automatically for a bad index.
Print the quantity inside the try block, after the access succeeds.

extra_fields.input_format:
First line: integer N.
Second line: N space-separated quantities.
Third line: requested index K.
extra_fields.output_format: Print Quantity: <value> or Invalid shelf index.

questions.title: Payment Terminal Cleanup
questions.objective: Use a finally block for cleanup that must run after both success and failure.
questions.problem_statement:
A payment terminal must perform cleanup regardless of whether a transaction succeeds. Simulate this behavior in memory without connecting to an actual payment service.

Create a method processPayment(boolean shouldFail). If shouldFail is true, the method must throw an IllegalStateException with the message Payment failed. Otherwise, it returns normally.

The main program reads 0 or 1, calls the method inside a try block, and prints Payment successful when it returns normally. Catch IllegalStateException and print its message. In a finally block, print Terminal reset.

The reset message must appear exactly once for both successful and failed transactions. Do not print a stack trace or exit the program before finally executes.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, including custom exceptions, without the public keyword.

Explanation: The payment method throws an exception. The catch block reports the failure, and the finally block resets the terminal afterward.

questions.output_format:
For success:
Payment successful
Terminal reset
For failure:
Payment failed
Terminal reset

hints: Throw the exception with throw new IllegalStateException("Payment failed");.
Print Payment successful on the line after the method call, still inside try; it is skipped if the call throws.
The finally block runs after try or catch, whichever finished.

extra_fields.output_format:

Terminal reset

Payment failed
Terminal reset

questions.title: Handle Errors in a Logistics Calculator
questions.objective: Handle two exception types in one multi-catch clause and tell them apart by type.
questions.problem_statement:
A logistics application calculates either a delivery ratio or a selected route value. It receives an operation code and two integers, A and B.
- Operation 1: calculate the integer quotient A / B.
- Operation 2: create an array containing exactly one element, A, and retrieve the element at index B.
- Any other operation code: print Invalid operation.
For operation 1, a zero divisor must result in Division by zero. For operation 2, any index other than 0 must result in Invalid route index. Handle ArithmeticException and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException using a Java multi-catch clause. Because the two exceptions require different messages, use the caught exception's type to select the correct message.

Print only one output line. Unsupported operation codes must be handled with ordinary conditional logic, not by throwing an unrelated exception.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, including custom exceptions, without the public keyword.

Explanation: Operation 1 requests integer division. The divisor is zero, so ArithmeticException is caught by the multi-catch clause and reported as a division error.
questions.input_format: One line containing three space-separated integers: operation code, A, and B.
questions.output_format: Print the calculation result or the appropriate error message.
hints: A multi-catch clause lists both types: catch (ArithmeticException | ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException e).
Inside it, use e instanceof ArithmeticException to choose the message.
Handle unsupported codes with an if statement before or outside the try block.

extra_fields.input_format: One line containing three space-separated integers: operation code, A, and B.
extra_fields.output_format: Print the calculation result or the appropriate error message.

questions.title: Shopping Cart Price Calculation
questions.objective: Accumulate a total with Math.multiplyExact() and Math.addExact(), reporting overflow instead of wrapping.
questions.problem_statement:
An online shopping cart calculates the combined price of multiple products. Read the number of products, followed by each product's unit price in paise and quantity. Calculate each line total and the grand total using long.

A unit price must be positive, and a quantity must be positive. Read and validate all products first: if any value violates these rules, print Invalid product details and do not calculate a total. Otherwise, use Math.multiplyExact() for each line total and Math.addExact() when accumulating the grand total. If either operation overflows, catch ArithmeticException and print Cart total overflow.

If every product is valid and all calculations fit in a long, print the grand total. The calculation must not silently wrap around when a value becomes too large.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, including custom exceptions, without the public keyword.

Explanation: The line totals are 200, 750, and 500 paise. Their sum is 1450 paise.
questions.input_format:
First line: integer N, the number of products.
Next N lines: two space-separated integers, unit price in paise and quantity.
questions.output_format: Print Cart total: <total> on success. Otherwise, print Invalid product details or Cart total overflow.
questions.constraints:
1 ≤ N ≤ 1000
Each price and quantity is a valid Java long value.
hints: Store the prices and quantities in long arrays so validation can finish before any calculation.
Invalid product details takes priority: check every product before multiplying.
Wrap the whole calculation loop in one try block; the first overflow jumps straight to the catch.

questions.title: Employee Leave Eligibility
questions.objective: Combine a custom checked exception with an unchecked one and catch each separately.
questions.problem_statement:
An HR system checks whether an employee has enough available leave days to submit a leave request. Create a custom checked exception named InsufficientLeaveException that extends Exception.

Implement validateLeave(int availableDays, int requestedDays) with throws InsufficientLeaveException. Apply these rules:
1. If either value is negative, or the requested days are zero, throw IllegalArgumentException with the message Invalid leave details.
2. If the requested days exceed the available days, throw InsufficientLeaveException with the message Insufficient leave balance.
3. Otherwise, return normally.
In main(), catch both exception types separately. Print Leave request approved if the method returns normally. Otherwise, print the relevant exception message. The available balance is not changed by this validation program.

This question tests the compiler-enforced handling of a checked exception, not merely the production of an error message.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, including custom exceptions, without the public keyword.

Explanation: The employee requests 15 days but has only 12 available. The method throws InsufficientLeaveException, and the caller prints its message.

questions.output_format: Print Leave request approved, Invalid leave details, or Insufficient leave balance.
hints: IllegalArgumentException is unchecked, so it doesn't need to appear in the throws clause; InsufficientLeaveException does.
Check rule 1 before rule 2.
Use two catch blocks after the same try.

extra_fields.output_format: Print Leave request approved, Invalid leave details, or Insufficient leave balance.

questions.title: Import a Batch of Employee Records

If the record has the wrong number of fields, contains malformed numeric data, or fails validation, print Record <number>: Import failed. Otherwise, print Record <number>: Imported. Handle parsing errors with NumberFormatException and continue processing later records.

questions.title: ATM Withdrawal Processing

questions.title: Process a Payment With Exception Propagation
questions.objective: Let a checked exception propagate through an intermediate method by declaring it with throws.
questions.problem_statement:
A payment service receives a transaction amount and a payment status. The payment processor may fail, and its exception must propagate through the service layer to the main program.

Create a custom checked exception named PaymentException that extends Exception. Implement processPayment(long amount, int status) with throws PaymentException.

The amount must be positive. If it is not, throw IllegalArgumentException with the message Invalid payment amount. If status is 1, throw PaymentException with the message Payment declined. If status is 0, return normally. Any other status must produce IllegalArgumentException with the message Invalid payment status.

Call processPayment() from a second method named submitOrder(long amount, int status). This method must declare throws PaymentException and must not catch that exception. In main(), catch PaymentException and IllegalArgumentException separately. Print Order confirmed on success or the relevant error message on failure.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, including custom exceptions, without the public keyword.

questions.output_format: Print Order confirmed, Invalid payment amount, Payment declined, or Invalid payment status.

Amount is a valid Java long value.
Status is an integer.
hints: Check the amount before the status.
submitOrder only calls processPayment; adding throws PaymentException to its header lets the exception pass through.
Remove the throws clause from submitOrder and the code no longer compiles, which shows that the exception is checked.

extra_fields.output_format: Print Order confirmed, Invalid payment amount, Payment declined, or Invalid payment status.

questions.title: Validate a Booking Date

February has 29 days in a leap year and 28 days otherwise. A leap year is divisible by 400, or divisible by 4 but not by 100.

If the date is invalid, throw InvalidDateException with the message Invalid booking date. Otherwise, return normally. The main program must catch the exception and print Booking date accepted on success or the exception message on failure.

Do not use a date-parsing library to replace the required validation logic.

questions.title: Preserve Payment Failure Causes

questions.title: Import Employee Records Without Stopping the Batch
questions.objective: Combine parsing errors and a custom validation exception in per-record handling.
questions.problem_statement:
A company imports employee records from a text-based data feed. Each record contains an employee ID, a name, and a monthly salary separated by the | character. The program must accept valid records and reject malformed records independently.

Create a custom checked exception named InvalidEmployeeException that extends Exception. Implement validateEmployee(int id, String name, long salary). It must throw InvalidEmployeeException with the message Invalid employee record if the ID is not positive, the name is blank after trimming, or the salary is negative. Salary zero is valid.

A record is malformed if it does not contain exactly two | characters, if the ID or salary cannot be parsed, or if either numeric field has surrounding whitespace. Do not trim the numeric fields before parsing. The name may contain spaces but cannot contain |; trim it before checking whether it is blank.

For each record, print Record <number>: Imported when it is valid. Otherwise, print Record <number>: Import failed. Parsing errors and validation exceptions must not stop the remaining records from being processed.

Read the record count with Integer.parseInt(sc.nextLine()) before reading the records as complete lines. This avoids accidentally consuming the first record when using Scanner.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, including custom exceptions, without the public keyword.

Explanation: Record 1 is valid. Record 2 has a non-positive ID. Record 3 has a blank name. Record 4 has a positive ID, a valid name, and a non-negative salary, so it is accepted.

First line: integer N.
Next N lines: one record per line in the format id|name|salary.
questions.output_format: Print one import-status line for each record, using one-based record numbering.
questions.constraints:
1 ≤ N ≤ 1000
Each record line contains at most 200 characters.
Valid IDs fit in the Java int range.
Valid salaries fit in the Java long range.

Record 1: Imported
Record 2: Import failed
Record 3: Import failed
Record 4: Imported

Treat a wrong field count as a failure too; checking parts.length != 3 before parsing handles it.

questions.title: Retry a Failed API Request
questions.objective: Catch a recurring exception inside a retry loop and throw a checked exception when attempts run out.
questions.problem_statement:
An application communicates with a service that may temporarily fail. Simulate the retry behavior without using an actual network, external service, thread, or delay.

Create a custom checked exception named RetryLimitExceededException that extends Exception. Implement performWithRetries(int failuresBeforeSuccess, int maxAttempts) with throws RetryLimitExceededException.

The simulated request has an attempt counter starting at zero. Each attempt increments the counter. If the attempt number is less than or equal to failuresBeforeSuccess, the request throws an IllegalStateException with the message Temporary service failure. Otherwise, the request succeeds.

For every failed attempt, print Attempt <number>: Temporary service failure. For the successful attempt, print Attempt <number>: Success and stop immediately.

If every permitted attempt fails, throw RetryLimitExceededException with the message Retry limit exceeded. The caller must catch it and print its message after all failed-attempt lines.

If failuresBeforeSuccess = maxAttempts - 1, the request must succeed on the last permitted attempt. If failuresBeforeSuccess >= maxAttempts, all attempts must fail. The program must never perform more than maxAttempts attempts.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, including custom exceptions, without the public keyword.

Explanation: The first two attempts fail because their attempt numbers are at most 2. The third attempt succeeds, so the application stops retrying.
questions.input_format: One line containing two integers: F, the number of failures before success, and A, the maximum number of attempts.
questions.output_format: Print one line per attempt. If all attempts fail, print Retry limit exceeded after the attempt lines.
sample_outputs:
Attempt 1: Temporary service failure
Attempt 2: Temporary service failure
Attempt 3: Success
hints: Write a helper that performs one attempt and throws IllegalStateException when the attempt number is at most F.
Loop over attempts 1 to A; catch the exception inside the loop, print the failure, and continue.
Return as soon as an attempt succeeds; if the loop finishes, throw RetryLimitExceededException.

questions.title: Update Warehouse Inventory Safely
questions.objective: Validate signed long updates without overflow, including Long.MIN_VALUE, and keep state unchanged on failure.
questions.problem_statement:
A warehouse system processes stock increases and decreases. Each stock update must either succeed completely or leave the existing inventory unchanged.

Create a custom checked exception named InvalidInventoryOperationException that extends Exception. Create an Inventory class that stores the current quantity as a long and provides update(long change), declaring throws InvalidInventoryOperationException.

Apply these rules:
1. If change is zero, throw InvalidInventoryOperationException with the message Change cannot be zero.
2. If change is negative and the requested removal exceeds the current quantity, throw InvalidInventoryOperationException with the message Insufficient inventory.
3. If change is positive and adding it would exceed Long.MAX_VALUE, throw ArithmeticException with the message Inventory overflow.
4. Otherwise, update the quantity and return normally.
Do not modify the quantity until all checks have passed. Do not use Math.abs(change) to determine the magnitude of a negative change, because Math.abs(Long.MIN_VALUE) remains negative due to overflow. Since the stored quantity is non-negative, a safe check is to compare the negative change against -quantity.

The main program processes each update independently. On success, print the updated quantity. On failure, print the exception message and preserve the previous quantity. Continue processing later requests.

Additional edge cases:
- Starting with quantity 10 and applying Long.MIN_VALUE must print Insufficient inventory.
- Starting with quantity 9223372036854775800 and adding 10 must print Inventory overflow.
- A zero change must print Change cannot be zero.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, including custom exceptions, without the public keyword.

Explanation: The quantity increases from 10 to 15, then decreases to 12. Removing 20 would make the inventory negative, so that update fails without changing the quantity. The final update succeeds, leaving 14.
questions.input_format:
First line: initial inventory quantity.
Second line: integer Q.
Third line: Q space-separated signed long changes.
questions.output_format: For each request, print Updated: <quantity> after success, or the applicable error message after failure.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ initial quantity ≤ 9,000,000,000,000,000,000
1 ≤ Q ≤ 1000
Each change is a valid Java long value.
hints: For a negative change, the removal is too large when change < -quantity; -quantity never overflows because quantity is non-negative.
For a positive change, adding overflows when change > Long.MAX_VALUE - quantity.
Catch InvalidInventoryOperationException and ArithmeticException inside the loop and print getMessage().
